repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: OpenDoor is an OWASP-oriented CLI Web Recon & Directory Discovery Platform for authorized security work. Documentation and agent work should describe it as a context-aware reconnaissance platform, not only as a basic directory brute-forcer. Core areas include dictionary-based directory discovery, subdomain enumeration, fingerprint-first scanning, WAF detection, response sniffers, response filtering, report generation, session resume, CI/CD fail-on buckets, report diffing, proxy support, OpenVPN/WireGuard transports, and controlled authorized bypass probes.

repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: The most important documentation outcome is to explain how targets are normalized and discovered, how scan dictionaries and remote/custom wordlists are used, how fingerprints and WAF signals influence operator decisions, how response buckets and sniffers classify evidence, how filters and auto-calibration reduce false positives, how transport/proxy settings affect execution, and how JSON/HTML/SARIF/SQLite reports support audit, automation, and release-to-release exposure validation.

repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: Repository documentation should explicitly cover docs/, src/, tests/, data/, examples/, scripts/, .github/e2e/, benchmarks/, dictionaries, signatures, report formats, sniffer behavior, fingerprint technologies, release tooling, and packaging files. These areas are essential for understanding scanner coverage, runtime behavior, validation strategy, and distribution workflows.

repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: The Mastering OpenDoor article series has started. Part 1 is published on Medium and the project has an official ReadTheDocs companion page plus a deterministic local lab under examples/mastering-lab. Keep Part 1 links in README and docs/guides/mastering-opendoor.md. Do not start Part 2 yet; it is intentionally deferred until after the next release, planned roughly one week later.

repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: When suggesting repository changes, preserve current CLI behavior unless the maintainer explicitly approves a public change. Follow the repository's AGENTS.md rules: assess blast radius, protect existing output/report semantics, add deterministic unittest coverage for runtime changes, keep packaging distribution-friendly, and run the documented validation commands relevant to the change.

repo_notes.author: Stanislav WEB
repo_notes.content: Avoid framing OpenDoor as an anonymity or bypass tool. Proxy, OpenVPN, WireGuard, WAF-safe mode, and controlled header/path bypass features must be described as authorized testing and transport/routing workflows. Do not suggest aggressive scans, hidden request-volume behavior, credential submission, or third-party target scanning without explicit authorization.
